transcript.text: Can you describe your experience assisting in a thin-film measurement experiment during your summer internship?

I'm a final-year BSc Physics student. Last summer I spent eight weeks as an intern at a national research institute, helping with a thin-film measurement experiment. My job was to record readings, about 120 in all, and plot them. I enjoyed the work but realised that I like asking why a lab's equipment is bought and how projects are chosen more than the experiments. That is why I want an MBA.

You mentioned you enjoy understanding how projects are chosen and why equipment is bought. Can you explain what aspects of these decisions interest you the most and how you have explored this curiosity so far?

transcript.text: As secretary of the Physics Association I ran six weekly problem-solving sessions for juniors. Attendance was low at first, so I moved them to the evening after classes and it improved.

feedback.summary: The candidate effectively linked their internship experience to their motivation for pursuing an MBA, showing introspection about their interests beyond technical work. They demonstrated initiative and problem-solving skills in their role as Physics Association secretary by adjusting session timings to improve attendance. However, there were inconsistencies regarding their internship role, and some responses lacked detailed reasoning and exploration of alternatives. Future practice should focus on clarifying responsibilities and decision-making processes with specific examples.
